title: Tenant-aware rate adjuster and deadline fallback to reduce hosted 5xx waves during customer escalations
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Summary: During a recent customer escalation (high-volume tenant upload + aggressive client retries) we observed multi-tenant 5xx spikes originating in the hosted inference path. Root cause appears to be repeated retry amplification combined with long-lived streaming requests holding inference slots and increasing KV cache eviction pressure. This ticket implements a tenant-aware rate adjuster at the front door plus a per-request deadline fallback so overloaded tenants receive graceful degradation instead of amplifying 5xx waves.

Why this is different from previous fixes: Prior work focused on connection pooling, circuit breakers, and tenant quarantine. This approach proactively adjusts admitted request rate by tenant based on real-time backend admission metrics and enforces a soft per-request deadline that triggers a structured fallback (cached prefix or short-response) rather than unbounded retries. The goal is to stop amplification cycles earlier and preserve capacity for healthy tenants while reducing overall customer-visible 5xxs.

Hypothesis: If we limit admitted concurrency per-tenant based on backend queue depth and attach a deadline-driven fallback that returns a short, explainable degraded response (or an explicit retry-after) the backend will avoid cascading failures, KV cache thrashing will reduce, and total 5xx incidence will drop by >60% for tenant surge scenarios.
repro_steps:
1) Simulate a tenant with bursty upload of long-sequence streaming requests (seq len ~8k tokens) while enabling SDK aggressive retries (interval 100ms, max 10).
2) Observe admission queues on hosted inference pool, KV cache eviction rate, and edge request fanout.
3) Verify 5xx tail increases and other tenants experience elevated latency/5xx.
4) Run same scenario with feature-flagged tenant-rate-adjuster enabled and per-request deadline set to 6s and compare metrics.
mitigation:
Immediate: deploy edge-side temporary soft-throttling per tenant (rate cap 30 rps) and turn on circuit-breaker hysteresis for long-running streaming sessions; communicate to on-call and affected customer with recommended client-side backoff.
Short-term (this ticket): implement tenant-aware rate adjuster + deadline fallback behind a feature flag with Canary rollout to 5% of tenants.
Long-term: calibrate adaptive admission using model-level cost heuristics + surface per-tenant recommended SDK backoff config in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Feature flag exists and can be toggled per-tenant
Canary rollout (5% tenants) shows >=60% reduction in hosted-api 5xx for synthetic surge tests
No measurable increase in error rate for unaffected tenants during canary
Dashboard exposes admission decisions and per-tenant deadline-triggered fallbacks
